recipes.name: Ouzo with Water
recipes.geographyNote: Traditional Greek ouzo serve, not an invented shaken cocktail

versions.label: Visit Greece · traditional serve
versions.instructions: Pour ouzo into a small glass and slowly add chilled water to taste. It turns cloudy as the anise oils disperse; ice is optional.
versions.history: Ouzo is Greece's anise-flavored aperitif, traditionally sipped slowly with water and meze. Its clouding when diluted is characteristic of anise spirits.

recipes.instructions: Pour ouzo into a small glass and slowly add chilled water to taste. It turns cloudy as the anise oils disperse; ice is optional.

recipes.name: Baijiu Sour
recipes.geographyNote: China-inspired baijiu cocktail; the article does not establish that this specific recipe originated in China

versions.label: Chinese American Family · Baijiu Sour
versions.instructions: Dry shake the egg white, then shake vigorously with the other ingredients and ice. Strain into a rocks glass, without double-straining, and finish with the bitters.
versions.history: This modern sour introduces baijiu, China's distinctive grain spirit, to a familiar citrus-and-egg-white cocktail structure. It is China-inspired rather than a verified Chinese-origin classic.

recipes.instructions: Dry shake the egg white, then shake vigorously with the other ingredients and ice. Strain into a rocks glass, without double-straining, and finish with the bitters.
